## Intent
Hypothesis: compiler auto-vectorization over per-particle components can approach the streaming ceiling on low-churn workloads.

## Cache saturation
At q=0.01, cost falls from 11.9 ns/p (N=4000) to 7.738 ns/p (N=65000) — overhead amortization at small N, not a cache effect, since N=4000 already exceeds the L1d spill at N≈910. The L2 spill at N≈58254 falls between N=16000 and N=65000; crossing it produces no knee — ns/p stays flat at ~7.7–7.9 from N=16000 through N=4000000. Death rate raises the floor without reshaping the curve: the large-N floor moves from ~7.8 ns/p (q=0.01) to ~8.6 (q=0.05) to ~11.9 (q=0.25), but the N-shape — overhead at small N, flat at large N — is preserved across all death rates. No cache-spill knee appears at any death rate.

## Bandwidth
Peak achieved bandwidth is 9.3 GB/s at N=65000, q=0.01 — 36.9% of the 25.22 GB/s streaming ceiling. At q=0.25 the peak falls to 6.03 GB/s (24% of ceiling). The algorithm never approaches bandwidth-bound behavior at any N or death rate; it is overhead- and compute-bound throughout. Bandwidth does not transition toward the ceiling as N grows — it plateaus at ~9 GB/s (q=0.01) once overhead amortizes, then slowly erodes at N≥1000000 for q=0.05. The gap to ceiling is consistent with the scalar scatter phase dominating execution time.

## Assembly
The compiler vectorized component-wise across one particle's fields, not across particles. The update loop uses `fmul.4s`/`fadd.4s` on 4-lane floats and `fmul.2s`/`fadd.2s` on 2-lane floats, with `ext.16b v18, v16, v17, #0xc` to rearrange components and `ld1.s {v17}[1], [x11]` as an indexed single-element gather. The deposit/scatter phase is entirely scalar: 16 `strb` and 12 `ldrb` instructions with `csel` clamping to 0xff. These byte-granular random stores cannot stream, explaining why bandwidth caps at 37% of ceiling despite the vectorized update loop.

## Verdict
Refuted — peak bandwidth never exceeds 9.3 GB/s (37% of the 25.22 GB/s ceiling) at q=0.01, N=65000, and falls to 6.03 GB/s (24%) at q=0.25. Component-wise auto-vectorization exists (`fmul.4s`, `fadd.4s`) but the scalar byte-granular scatter (16 `strb`, 12 `ldrb`) dominates, preventing the algorithm from approaching the streaming ceiling at any death rate.
